question.text: 'Krishna Venture AIF' (Cat I VCF) is a regular (non-Angel) scheme. What is the maximum number of investors it can have per scheme under SEBI AIF Regulations?

explanation.text: The Logic: An AIF scheme (other than Angel Funds) cannot have more than 1,000 investors, and accredited investors are excluded from this count. The Companies Act private-placement regime separately caps offerings at 200 — but where the AIF is not constituted as a company, the AIF Regulation cap of 1,000 governs. The Trap: 200 is the Companies Act private-placement cap, not the ordinary AIF scheme cap. 500 has no regulatory basis. 'Unlimited' is wrong — SEBI prescribes a hard cap. Note: Angel Fund onboarding under current rules is structured around accredited investors; the historical 200-investor framing for Angel Funds should be checked against the latest applicable SEBI circulars before being applied.
